docs.title: rapid-cp-schema
docs.text:
LinkML schema for RAPID TA1 computable phenotypes (CPs): versioned, data-model-independent CP logic files.

  • Auto-generated schema documentation
  • Applying RAPID CP files in OMOP 5.4: what each field means, and how a site turns a CP into counts
  • The results-file specification (v1.1): the counts file each site returns to Mendelian

The schema was drafted by Mendelian as rapid-cp-logic v0.1.0 and is being moved here, to a programme-neutral home for RAPID TA1.

docs.title: Applying RAPID CP files in OMOP 5.4
docs.text: What a computable phenotype (CP) file contains, and how a site applies it to OMOP CDM 5.4 data. Written by Mendelian for the sites that run RAPID CPs.

docs.title: 1. About this document
docs.text:
Mendelian shares each computable phenotype (CP) as a YAML file. Each site turns it into queries on its own OMOP CDM 5.4 data, runs them, and returns counts in the format set by the Results-File Specification.

  • What a site receives. One CP file per CP version. The files follow this repository's LinkML schema, rapid_cp_schema.yaml. Its versions and what changed in each are listed in the changelog.
  • What is fixed. What a CP file means: which evidence each feature describes and how features combine into a flag (sections 3 to 5).
  • What each site decides. How it searches its data for that evidence. Section 7 gives Mendelian's recommendations for OMOP 5.4. They reflect how Mendelian applies the files, but each site knows its own data best. A site that departs from them should tell Mendelian how, so results can be compared across sites.
  • What a site returns. One results file per execution, as the Results-File Specification describes. Section 8 shows how a CP's logic maps onto its rows.

A CP file never contains OMOP concept ids. Every code is written in its source vocabulary (ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm) and is looked up in the site's own vocabulary tables.

docs.title: 2. The files
docs.text:
Each CP version is one YAML file named after its cp_name, for example RAPID000123-xlh_L2A_v2.0.yaml.

RAPID000123-xlh_L2A_v2.0 Meaning RAPID000123 The disease entity's id (disease.disease_entity_id): RAPID followed by exactly six digits -xlh A short name for the disease (disease.slug) _L2A The level: L1, L2A, L2B or L3 (section 5) _v2 Major version: goes up when the CP's structure changes, such as a criterion added or removed or the level changed .0 Minor version: goes up when details inside the structure change, such as codes, thresholds or points

Everything in the name after the disease entity id is lowercase except the level, so two names can't differ only in case and collide on a case-insensitive file system.

The disease entity id is opaque: it says nothing about the disease, and it does not depend on Mondo. Mendelian mints one id per disease entity. Every CP for that entity carries the same id, across levels and versions. A change to Mondo, such as the anchor Mondo id being obsoleted or merged, doesn't change the id. Only a change to the disease entity itself does: when an entity is split, each resulting entity gets a new id; when entities are merged, the merged entity gets a new id. In both cases the old ids are retired. An id is never reused or given to another entity.

Names starting cluster- are reserved for future cluster CPs. They will be named cluster-<umbrella-code>_<level>_v<major>.<minor>, with the umbrella code lowercase, prefixed with its vocabulary and without dots, e.g. cluster-icd10e833_L2A_v1.0.

  • Versions are separate files. A new version never overwrites an old one. Mendelian tracks which versions are published; sites run only published versions.
  • The schema. rapid_cp_schema.yaml defines every field and allowed value. The schema documentation describes each class and field.
  • Reading the YAML. Codes, dates and version numbers are quoted ("82236004", "2026-09-24"), so they should be read as text, not numbers or dates. A code can otherwise lose a leading zero.

Which part of the version goes up depends on what changed:

  • Major (v1.3 → v2.0): the structure changes. A disjunct, rule or score item is added or removed, the level changes, the search mode or cluster changes, or a feature's module changes. Major numbers are never reused.
  • Minor (v1.0 → v1.1): the structure stays the same but details inside it change. For example, codes are added to or removed from a feature, a threshold or min_distinct_dates changes, or score points are re-weighted. Minor goes back to 0 on a major bump.
  • Neither: only fields that don't affect which patients are flagged change: title, review, provenance, expected_flag_rate, notes and absorbed_into.

docs.title: 3. Top-level fields
docs.text:
Only the fields marked query change which patients are flagged. The rest describe the CP and its history; they can be read but aren't needed to build queries.

Field Required Used by queries Meaning cp_name yes no The CP version's name (section 2). schema_version yes no Version of the LinkML schema the file follows, e.g. 0.2.0. title yes no A readable name for the CP. disease yes no The disease entity: disease_entity_id (the RAPID id in cp_name), mondo_id (primary Mondo id), slug, name, included_mondo_ids (every Mondo id for the entity, primary included), curation_record_version. level yes query L1, L2A, L2B or L3. Decides which logic block the file carries (section 5). search_mode yes query population: search everyone. cluster: search only patients with an umbrella code (section 5.5). cluster in cluster mode query umbrella_codes: the codes that define the group searched. candidate_mondo_ids: documentation only. features yes query The evidence (section 4). disjuncts, rules or score one, by level query The logic (section 5). A file carries only its own level's block. provenance yes no authored_by, authored_date, kg_extracted_at, change_note, supersedes (the version this one replaces). review no no Clinical sign-off: reviewer, date, decision (proceed or revise), comments. expected_flag_rate no no The range of patients per 100,000 a correct CP should flag: low_per_100k, high_per_100k, basis, source. Mendelian compares each site's results against it. absorbed_into no no Reserved for future cluster CPs. notes no no Free text.

docs.title: 4. Features
docs.text:
A feature is one piece of evidence: a set of codes, plus, for tests and measurements, the result that must be found. A feature listed under features but not used by the logic is carried for the record only and needs no query.

Field Required Meaning id yes f1, f2, … Referenced by the logic. module yes The kind of evidence (table below). name yes A readable name, e.g. "Low serum phosphate". specificity_grade yes S1 (confirmatory) to S5 (incidental) (4.4). Level 1 uses only S1 features. codes yes One or more code references. A record matching any one of them counts. result tests and measured phenotypes The result that must be found (4.2). genetic genetic findings The gene and accepted interpretations (4.3). include_personal_history no Diagnoses and coded phenotypes only. Default true: a record of the patient's own history of the condition also counts (section 7.3). hpo_id no The HPO term a phenotype represents. Annotation only. text_terms no Names and synonyms for a future text search. Not used for structured queries. Module Vocabularies Needs diagnostic_code ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT — phenotype (coded) ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT — phenotype (measured) LOINC result diagnostic_test LOINC, SNOMED CT result; an order alone never counts genetic_finding LOINC, SNOMED CT genetic medication RxNorm — procedure SNOMED CT —

docs.title: 4.1 Code references
docs.text:
Each entry under codes is written like {vocabulary: SNOMED, code: "82236004", label: ..., include_descendants: true}.

Field Meaning vocabulary ICD10CM, SNOMED, LOINC or RXNORM, plus UCUM for result units only. In OMOP these are the vocabulary_id values ICD10CM, SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm and UCUM. code The code as written in that vocabulary, e.g. E83.31. Matches OMOP's concept_code. ICD-10-CM codes are dotted; one written without the dot, such as E8331, is read as E83.31. label Optional, for readers. include_descendants Also match the more specific codes beneath it. Default true for a feature's codes, false for result values and units.

docs.title: 4.2 Results
docs.text:
A numeric result compares the record's value with a threshold; a qualitative one accepts listed answers.

Operator Matches when the value is… Needs gt / gte above (or equal to) value value lt / lte below (or equal to) value value between from value to value_high, both included both above_ref_high above the upper limit of the normal range recorded with that result — below_ref_low below the lower limit of the normal range recorded with that result —
  • units: UCUM units the threshold applies to, e.g. {vocabulary: UCUM, code: mg/dL}. With none given, values in any unit are compared. The reference-range operators are usually the safer choice: they need no units and are age-appropriate wherever the lab supplies ranges.
  • value_concepts (qualitative only): the accepted answers, e.g. LOINC LA6576-8 (Positive).

docs.title: 4.3 Genetic findings
docs.text:
• gene_symbol (required): the causal gene, e.g. PHEX. hgnc_id: optional reference.
  • interpretations: accepted answers, e.g. LOINC LA6668-3 (Pathogenic), LA26332-9 (Likely pathogenic).
  • require_gene_text_match: the gene symbol must appear in the record's text. Default true when the codes are generic LOINC panels.

Any variant in the gene with an accepted interpretation counts; a CP can't name specific variants.

docs.title: 4.4 Specificity grades
docs.text:
The grade says how specific a feature is to the target disease. It decides what counts as safe alone at Level 1. The examples are for XLH and are illustrative, not clinically reviewed.

Grade Meaning Example S1 Confirmatory: a patient with this feature almost certainly has the disease. Only S1 features may be Level 1 disjuncts. Burosumab S2 Highly specific: only a small number of other conditions produce this feature. ICD-10-CM E83.31, familial hypophosphatemia, which also covers other inherited forms S3 Suggestive: the feature narrows the differential diagnosis but doesn't settle it. Low serum phosphate S4 Weak: the feature says almost nothing about the disease on its own. Short stature S5 Incidental: the feature is common in the disease but is not evidence for it. Knee pain

docs.title: 5. Logic
docs.text: The level decides how features combine. Each part of the logic has an id (d1, r2, s3…); these are the criteria a site reports counts for. Level 3 can be declared but has no logic block yet, so sites don't receive L3 files to run.

docs.title: 5.1 Level 1: disjuncts
docs.text:
A patient is flagged if any disjunct is met. Each disjunct names one S1 feature.

disjuncts:
  - {id: d1, feature: f1}
  - {id: d2, feature: f2, min_distinct_dates: 2}

docs.title: 5.2 Level 2A: rules
docs.text:
A patient is flagged if any rule's condition holds. Each rule has an id (r1…), an optional label, and an expr. Conditions nest as deeply as needed, and every rule contains at least one feature that isn't negated, because a rule made only of none_of would match almost everyone.

Form True when Example feature The feature is present, meeting any date options (5.4) {feature: f3, min_distinct_dates: 2} all_of Every listed condition holds {all_of: [{feature: f2}, {feature: f5}]} any_of At least one listed condition holds {any_of: [{feature: f3}, {feature: f4}]} none_of None of the listed conditions holds {none_of: [{feature: f9}]} at_least + of At least N of the listed conditions hold {at_least: 2, of: [{feature: f2}, {feature: f3}, {feature: f4}]} within A record of each listed feature, all within days of each other {within: {days: 365, of: [f2, f5]}}

With within: {..., in_order: true}, the records must also fall in the listed order: the first feature's record on or before the second's, and so on. Records on the same day count as in order, and days is measured from the first listed feature to the last. of lists feature ids only.

docs.title: 5.3 Level 2B: score
docs.text:
score:
  threshold: 4
  items:
    - {id: s1, feature: f2, points: 2}
    - {id: s2, feature: f3, points: 2, min_distinct_dates: 2}
    - {id: s3, feature: f9, points: -3}

Each item adds its points when its feature is present (meeting any date options); points can be negative. A patient is flagged when their total reaches threshold.

docs.title: 5.4 Date options
docs.text:
Any feature reference (a disjunct, a rule's feature, a score item) can add:

  • min_distinct_dates: the feature must appear on at least this many different days (default 1). Days are counted, not records, so duplicate records don't count twice.
  • min_span_days: the feature's records must stretch across at least this many days, from first to last. This separates a condition that keeps being recorded from a code entered once in error.

docs.title: 5.5 Cluster mode
docs.text: With search_mode: cluster, the first step finds every patient with any of cluster.umbrella_codes, searched like a diagnostic code with descendants included (e.g. E83.3 also covers E83.30, E83.31…), except that records of the patient's own history don't count. The logic is then evaluated only for those patients: a patient who meets a criterion but has no umbrella code is not flagged. Each candidate disease under an umbrella has its own CP file with the same umbrella codes.

docs.title: 5.6 Rules a valid CP file follows
docs.text:
A CP file that breaks any of these rules is wrong, even where the schema doesn't reject it yet.

The file as a whole

  • cp_name agrees with the file name, level, disease.disease_entity_id and disease.slug (section 2).
  • included_mondo_ids, when given, includes mondo_id.
  • supersedes, when given, is a cp_name.
  • schema_version is a schema version number, e.g. 0.2.0.
  • A cluster block is given when search_mode is cluster, and only then. Umbrella codes are ICD-10-CM or SNOMED CT.
  • Each level carries its own logic block and no other: disjuncts (at least one) for L1, rules for L2A, score for L2B, and none for L3.
  • expected_flag_rate: with basis: none, no numbers are given. Otherwise high_per_100k is required, low_per_100k may be left out for an open-ended range, and low_per_100k is not above high_per_100k.

Features

  • Feature ids are unique, and so are the ids of disjuncts, rules and score items, since each is reported as a criterion.
  • Every feature has at least one code, in a vocabulary its module allows (section 4). UCUM is used for result units only, and units are always UCUM.
  • SNOMED CT and RxNorm codes are quoted, so YAML doesn't read them as numbers.
  • result is given where the module needs it (diagnostic_test, measured phenotype) and not elsewhere; genetic is given on genetic_finding features only.
  • A phenotype feature with LOINC codes is all-LOINC. A coded (SNOMED CT or ICD-10-CM) phenotype goes in a separate feature.
  • include_personal_history is set only on diagnostic_code and coded phenotype features.
  • hpo_id is an HPO term (HP:…).
  • A numeric result has an operator and no value_concepts. gt, gte, lt and lte need a value; between needs value and value_high, with value not above value_high; above_ref_high and below_ref_low take neither. value_high is used only with between.
  • A qualitative result has value_concepts and no operator.

Logic

  • Every disjunct, rule leaf, score item and within.of entry names a feature listed under features.
  • Every disjunct names an S1 feature.
  • Each expr node is exactly one of the forms in section 5.2. at_least and of come together, and at_least is not more than the number of conditions in of. Lists of conditions are not empty.
  • min_distinct_dates and min_span_days are set on a feature reference only, not on a node that combines conditions.
  • within.of lists at least two feature ids.
  • Every rule has at least one feature that isn't under none_of (section 5.2).

docs.title: 6. Applying a CP in OMOP 5.4
docs.text:
A CP becomes counts in six steps. Steps 1 and 3 follow Mendelian's recommendations in section 7; the others follow directly from the CP file.

  1. Resolve the codes. For each feature, look up its codes in the site's CONCEPT table by vocabulary_id and concept_code, and add the descendants where include_descendants applies. Do the same separately for result answers (value_concepts, interpretations) and units, and for a cluster CP the umbrella codes. Each feature's concept lists stay separate.
  2. Apply cluster mode. For a cluster CP, find the patients with an umbrella code first (5.5), and search for features only among them. The result is the same, and the searches run over far fewer patients.
  3. Find each feature's records. In the tables for the feature's module, find the records whose concept is in that feature's list and, where the feature has a result or a genetic block, whose value qualifies. Each match gives a patient and a date.
  4. Summarise by patient and feature. For each patient and feature, note the number of distinct dates, the first date and, where min_span_days is used, the days between the first and last record.
  5. Evaluate the logic. For each patient, decide which disjuncts or rules are met, or add up the score (section 5). A patient is flagged when the level's rule says so.
  6. Count. Count distinct flagged patients, and for each criterion the patients who meet it (section 8). The population is counted as the Results-File Specification defines it.

docs.title: 7. Recommended matching rules in OMOP 5.4
docs.text: These are recommendations and following them keeps results comparable across sites.

docs.title: 7.1 Where to search
docs.text:
Module Tables to search Date of a record diagnostic_code, phenotype (coded) condition_occurrence, observation condition_start_date, observation_date phenotype (measured), diagnostic_test, genetic_finding measurement, observation measurement_date, observation_date medication drug_exposure drug_exposure_start_date procedure procedure_occurrence procedure_date

Why observation too: OMOP files a record by its concept's domain, and many SNOMED CT findings belong to the Observation domain. A result using above_ref_high or below_ref_low should search measurement only, since only it records normal ranges.

docs.title: 7.2 Matching codes
docs.text:
• Both concept columns. A record should match when either its standard concept (*_concept_id) or its source concept (*_source_concept_id) is in the feature's list. This finds a SNOMED CT code where OMOP stores it and an ICD-10-CM code as the site recorded it.
  • Descendants of SNOMED CT, LOINC and RxNorm should come from the site's CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table. An RxNorm ingredient then matches every product containing it.
  • ICD-10-CM by prefix. ICD-10-CM isn't a standard vocabulary in OMOP, so its codes never appear in CONCEPT_ANCESTOR. Its hierarchy is built into the codes instead: E83.3 should match every ICD10CM concept whose concept_code starts with E83.3.
  • Raw ICD-10-CM strings. Some data loads leave the source concept id at 0. For ICD-10-CM codes, the raw condition_source_value and observation_source_value should also be compared, ignoring case, dots and spaces (e8331 matches E83.31).
  • Retired concepts. A code whose concept has an invalid_reason should still be matched, since older records may carry it. Sites should report such codes to Mendelian, so the CP can be updated.

docs.title: 7.3 History records
docs.text:
• The patient's own history counts (unless the feature sets include_personal_history: false). OMOP usually records "history of X" as an observation row whose observation_concept_id is a history concept and whose value_as_concept_id is X. Such rows should match when value_as_concept_id is in the feature's list and observation_concept_id is SNOMED CT 417662000 (History of clinical finding in subject) or a descendant. A site that uses another history concept should use it and tell Mendelian.
  • Family history never counts. It is stored the same way under a family-history concept. Since only observation_concept_id and the source column are matched for ordinary records, and value_as_concept_id only under a personal-history concept, a relative's diagnosis never flags the patient.

docs.title: 7.4 Results and genetic findings
docs.text:
• Numeric: compare value_as_number. Where units are given, unit_concept_id must also be one of them. above_ref_high and below_ref_low compare with the same row's range_high and range_low; a row with no range recorded doesn't match.
  • Qualitative: value_as_concept_id must be one of the value_concepts.
  • Genetic: if genetic findings are stored in OMOP, the record's concept is in the feature's codes, its value_as_concept_id is one of the interpretations, and, when require_gene_text_match is true, the gene symbol appears (ignoring case) in the record's text: measurement_source_value and value_source_value in measurement; observation_source_value, value_as_string and value_source_value in observation.

docs.title: 7.5 Counting dates
docs.text: Distinct dates are counted per patient and feature, not rows, so duplicate records don't count twice. Records found through history count like any other record.

docs.title: 8. Producing the results file
docs.text:
Each CP version a site runs becomes one result in the results file: one summary row and one count row per criterion. The Results-File Specification sets the columns, formats, small-number rules and checks; this section only says which CP values go where.

Results-file value From the CP cp_name The CP's cp_name, exactly as written summary row, count_value Distinct patients flagged by the CP summary row, population_n The population as the specification defines it (its section 4.1). For a cluster CP this is still the site population, not the number of patients with an umbrella code. count rows, criterion_id Every disjunct (d1…), rule (r1…) or score item (s1…) in the CP, including any that found nobody (0) count rows, count_value Patients meeting that criterion (below)

What a criterion's count means:

  • Level 1: patients who meet that disjunct.
  • Level 2A: patients for whom that rule holds.
  • Level 2B: flagged patients for whom that item applied, i.e. its feature was present and met any date options. Negative items count too, which shows when one was outweighed.
  • Cluster CPs: only patients with an umbrella code are counted, in every criterion and in the flagged total.

A patient who meets several criteria is counted under each, so criterion counts can add up to more than the flagged total; the summary row counts each patient once.

docs.title: 9. Before running, and open points
docs.text:
Mendelian recommends two quick checks before the first run of each CP version. Neither touches patient data.

  • Do the codes resolve? Look up every code in the CP in the site's CONCEPT table. Sites should report any code that isn't found, is retired (invalid_reason set) or, where descendants are wanted, isn't a standard concept. These explain a lower flag rate than expected.
  • Which vocabulary release is the site on? It's the vocabulary_version of the VOCABULARY row whose vocabulary_id is None. Sites should report it to Mendelian with their first results; the results file has no column for it yet.

Open points Mendelian is working on:

  • The Results-File Specification describes criteria for Level 1 and 2A only. Score items (s1…) for Level 2B CPs, and the checks that apply to them, still need adding.
  • For cluster CPs, the results file has no place yet for the number of patients with an umbrella code.
  • Genetic findings rely on variant results being stored as structured rows. Where they aren't, those features will find nobody, and the approach needs discussing with Mendelian.

docs.title: RAPID results-file specification v1.1
docs.text: The file each site returns to Mendelian after running RAPID computable phenotypes (CPs), and how Mendelian checks it. Written by Mendelian for the RAPID Tracking Database.

docs.title: 1. About this specification
docs.text:
This document is for the site team that runs RAPID CPs on its own data. It defines the one file a site sends back to Mendelian after each run: what goes in it, how it is delivered, and the reasons a file or a result can be rejected. How a CP's logic maps onto the file is described in Applying RAPID CP files in OMOP 5.4, section 8.

  • A results file reports the counts from running one or more CPs at a site. It contains counts only, never patient-level data.
  • A result is one CP version run at a site on one date. One file can hold many results, across many disease entities.
  • Each result is checked on its own. A problem with one result never blocks the others in the same file.
  • Versions. This is version 1.1. Every file states the version it follows (result_spec_version = 1.1). Mendelian will announce any new version, and will keep accepting the previous one for a transition period.
  • Changes from version 1.0. cp_name follows the new CP name format, which starts with the disease entity's RAPID id instead of its Mondo id (RAPID000123-xlh_L1_v1.0, not mondo0010619-xlh_L1_v1.0). The advice for "CP version not registered" (section 6) now points to the CP file instead of its cp_id. Nothing else changed. Version 1.0 is no longer accepted: only test results were sent under it, so there is no transition period.
  • Questions about this specification go to the Mendelian RAPID team.

docs.title: 2. Delivery
docs.text:
Each site sends its results files to Mendelian through the channel agreed with Mendelian.

  1. A CSV file. UTF-8, comma-separated, with one header row, as laid out in section 3. The file must arrive as a CSV, not converted to a spreadsheet format.
  2. One file per execution. Everything run in one go goes into one file, however many CP versions and disease entities that covers.
  3. A name that is easy to find again. For example rapid-results_<site>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv. Mendelian doesn't read the name, but it helps when a file is discussed.
  4. A file once sent is never replaced or withdrawn. A correction is sent as a new file (section 7). The files sent are the record of what the site reported.

Mendelian sends the site the reasons for anything rejected (section 6).

docs.title: 3. File layout
docs.text:
Each result is written as one summary row followed by one count row for every criterion in the CP: d1, d2… for an L1 CP, or r1, r2… for an L2A CP. Every criterion is included, even one that flagged nobody (count 0). The rows of one result share the same cp_name and run_date. Results can appear in any order.

Column Format Filled on Meaning site_code text every row The site code, as given by Mendelian. The same on every row. result_spec_version text every row 1.1 for this specification. The same on every row. generated_at date and time with timezone, ISO 8601 every row When this file was produced, for example 2026-10-15T09:30:00Z. The same on every row. cp_name text every row The CP version's cp_name, exactly as published, for example RAPID999999-test-disease-a_L1_v1.0. run_date date, YYYY-MM-DD every row The date the site ran this CP version. data_snapshot_date date, YYYY-MM-DD every row The date the site's data was last refreshed before the run. row_type summary or count every row Which kind of row this is. criterion_id text count rows The criterion ID from the CP: d1, d2… or r1, r2… Empty on summary rows. population_n whole number summary rows The number of people the CP was run against (section 4.1). Never hidden. population_basis observation_time, all_persons or other summary rows How the site defined the population (section 4.1). population_basis_note text summary rows when the basis is other A short description of the site's definition. count_value whole number, or empty every row On a summary row, the number of patients the CP flagged. On a count row, the number of patients matching that criterion. Empty when the count is hidden. count_status exact or suppressed every row suppressed when the site hides a count from 1 to 10 (section 4.3), otherwise exact.

A column stays empty where the table says it isn't filled. Extra columns are not allowed.

docs.title: 4.1 Population
docs.text:
Each result reports one population count: the number of people the CP was run against.

  • Default: everyone with any recorded observation time in the site's data, with population_basis = observation_time.
  • A site that can only count everyone in its person table uses all_persons.
  • Any other definition uses other, described in population_basis_note.

The population must be a whole number greater than 0, and at least as large as the number of patients flagged. RAPID may decide to unify this definition across sites.

docs.title: 4.2 Dates
docs.text:
• run_date is the day the site ran the CP version. It can't be later than generated_at, or earlier than the date the CP version was published.
  • data_snapshot_date is the day the site's data was last refreshed. It can't be later than run_date.
  • generated_at is the date and time the file was produced, with timezone. A resent correction must have a later generated_at than the file it corrects.

docs.title: 4.3 Counts and small numbers
docs.text:
• On the summary row, count_value is the number of distinct patients the CP flagged.
  • On each count row, count_value is the number of patients matching that criterion. A patient who matches several criteria is counted under each of them, so the criterion counts can add up to more than the flagged total. That is expected.
  • For an L1 CP, the flagged total can't be smaller than the largest criterion count, or larger than the sum of all criterion counts.
  • Hiding small numbers. Where a site's rules require it, the site may hide any count from 1 to 10: count_value is left empty and count_status is set to suppressed.
  • Zero is never hidden: it is written as 0 with count_status = exact.
  • "<=10", "≤10", "-1" or "10" never go in count_value. A hidden count is shown only by count_status.
  • Complementary suppression is the site's responsibility. If a hidden count could be worked out from the others, for example from the flagged total minus the other criterion counts, the site applies its own rules to hide what else is needed.

docs.title: 6. What Mendelian checks
docs.text:
A problem with the whole file rejects every result in it. A problem with one result rejects only that result, and the rest of the file still loads. Mendelian sends the site every reason, worded as below.

Applies to Reason given What to do Whole file File can't be read: not a CSV, or columns missing or extra Use the layout in section 3, saved as a CSV. Whole file Unknown specification version Set result_spec_version to 1.1. Whole file site_code, result_spec_version or generated_at differs between rows Use the same value on every row. Whole file Site code does not match the site that sent the file Put the site's own code in site_code. One result CP version not registered Check the cp_name spelling against the published CP file. If it's right, tell Mendelian. One result CP version is a draft Run only published CP versions. One result CP version appears more than once in the file for the same run date Report each CP version and run date once. One result Missing summary row, or more than one Give exactly one summary row per result. One result Population missing or zero Give the population as a whole number greater than 0. One result Population basis "other" without a description Fill in population_basis_note. One result Flagged count larger than the population Check both numbers. One result Flagged count below the largest criterion count (L1 only) Check the counts: everyone matching a criterion is flagged. One result Flagged count above the sum of the criterion counts (L1 only) Check the counts: every flagged patient matches at least one criterion. One result Run date later than the file date, or earlier than the CP version's publication Check run_date and generated_at. One result Data snapshot date missing or later than the run date Give the date the site's data was last refreshed. One result Hidden count written as a number, or a count marked suppressed with a value Leave count_value empty for hidden counts, and write zero as 0 exact. One result Older than current data This file was produced before, or at the same moment as, the one that gave the current result. Send a correction as a new file with a later generated_at (section 7).

Results for a CP version that Mendelian has since superseded or withdrawn are still accepted. Mendelian may follow up with the site about them.

docs.title: 7. Resending and re-running
docs.text:
Situation What to send What Mendelian does A result was rejected, or the site found a mistake A new file with the corrected result, the same run_date, and a later generated_at. It only needs the results being corrected. The corrected result replaces the earlier one, which stays on record. The site ran a CP version again on refreshed data A new file with the new run_date and data_snapshot_date. Both results are kept. The new one is a separate run. The site sent exactly the same file twice Nothing. The copy is recognised and ignored.

A correction is always sent as a new file. The original is never replaced or edited, because it is part of the record. A resent file must be regenerated, so it carries a new generated_at. An exact copy of a file Mendelian already received, even one that was rejected, is recorded as a duplicate and loads nothing, with the reason "identical to a file already rejected: regenerate the file before resending".

docs.title: 8. Checking a file before sending
docs.text:
The layout in section 3 is also available as a machine-readable Frictionless Table Schema, results-file-schema-v1.1.json, with the worked example from section 5 as results-example-v1.1.csv. The version 1.0 schema and example stay in the same folder for reference only. A file can be checked against the schema with the free Frictionless command-line tool:

frictionless validate rapid-results_test_site_1_2026-10-15.csv --schema results-file-schema-v1.1.json

This catches layout and format problems: column names, dates, number formats and allowed values. It doesn't check the rules that compare rows or need Mendelian's records, such as the flagged-count limits, duplicate results, or whether a CP version is registered. Those are checked when Mendelian loads the file (section 6).

docs.title: rapid_cp_schema
docs.text:
Schema for RAPID computable phenotype (CP) logic files, named <cp_name>.yaml, e.g. RAPID000123-xlh_L1_v1.0.yaml. Data-model-independent. Says WHAT counts as evidence (features, coded in source vocabularies: ICD10CM, SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, ...) and HOW the evidence combines (Level 1 disjuncts, Level 2a rules, Level 2b score). Every disjunct / rule / score item carries a stable id (d1, r2, s3) that is reported back as the flag reason.

URI: https://mendelian.co/schemas/rapid-cp-logic

Name: rapid_cp_schema

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Class Description ClinicalReview Expert sign-off on the disease and its criteria, before the CP is tested at a site. ClusterScope Limits the search to patients who have at least one of the umbrella codes. Every criterion is then evaluated only for those patients. CodeRef A code written as it appears in its source vocabulary, never as an OMOP concept_id. ComputablePhenotype One versioned CP. File name must equal cp_name + .yaml. CPProvenance Who wrote this CP version and when. DiseaseRef The disease entity a CP is for, identified by a RAPID disease entity id and an anchor Mondo id. Disjunct A Level 1 criterion: one S1 feature that is enough on its own to flag a patient. Its id is reported with the counts. ExpectedFlagRate Range of patients per 100,000 a correct CP should flag at a site. Expr One condition in a Level 2A rule. Each node uses exactly one form: feature, all_of, any_of, none_of (none of the listed conditions holds), at_least with of, or within. A rule must contain at least one feature that isn't under none_of. min_distinct_dates and min_span_days apply only to a feature node. Feature One piece of evidence: a set of codes for one module, plus the result or genetic finding that must be found where the module needs one. Logic blocks refer to features by id. GeneticCriterion The variant result a genetic_finding feature looks for: a causal gene and the interpretations that count, such as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. A record matches when it carries one of the feature's codes, its interpretation is one of those listed (if any are), and, when require_gene_text_match is true, the gene symbol appears in the record's text. ResultCriterion The result a test or measurement record must have to count: a numeric comparison or a set of accepted answers. Rule A Level 2A criterion: a Boolean condition over features. A patient is flagged if any rule holds; each rule's id is reported with the counts. ScoreItem A Level 2B score item: points added when its feature is present. Its id is reported with the counts. ScoreModel The Level 2B logic: a patient is flagged when the points of the items that apply add up to the threshold. Within A record of each listed feature, all falling within days of each other. With in_order, the records must also occur in the listed order (the same day counts as in order).

docs.title: Slots
docs.text: Slot Description absorbed_into The cluster CP that currently handles this disease, e.g. cluster-icd10n18x_L2A_v1.0. Empty once the disease stands alone. Cluster CPs themselves are not supported yet; the field and the cluster- naming are reserved so nothing needs renaming later. all_of any_of at_least authored_by authored_date basis candidate_mondo_ids Documentation only: the diseases under the umbrella. Not queried; each candidate gets its own CP. change_note Why this version exists (PR description summary). cluster Required if and only if search_mode is cluster. code codes comments cp_name Name of the CP version, built from the disease entity, level and version. Format: <disease_entity_id>-<slug>_<level>_v<major>.<minor>, where <disease_entity_id> is disease.disease_entity_id and <slug> is disease.slug, e.g. RAPID000123-xlh_L1_v1.0. curation_record_version Version of the curation record (keyed by mondo_id) this CP was built from. Recorded, not queried. date days decision disease disease_entity_id Opaque id of the disease entity, RAPID + exactly six digits, e.g. RAPID000123. Minted by Mendelian. Every CP for the entity carries the same id, across levels and versions. It does not depend on Mondo, so it stays the same when the anchor Mondo id is obsoleted or merged. disjuncts Level 1 only. expected_flag_rate expr feature features Atomic evidence items. Logic blocks reference them by id. gene_symbol genetic Required for genetic_finding features. hgnc_id high_per_100k Required unless basis is none. hpo_id Phenotype features: the HPO term this realises (annotation only, not queried). id in_order include_descendants Default true for a feature's main codes, false for result value and unit codes. SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm expand via CONCEPT_ANCESTOR; ICD10CM expands by code prefix. include_personal_history diagnostic_code and coded phenotype features only. Default true: also count observation rows recording the patient's own history of the condition. Set false to count only direct records. included_mondo_ids Every Mondo id that constitutes this disease entity, mondo_id included. Defaults to [mondo_id]. Recorded, not queried. interpretations items kg_extracted_at When Mendelian extracted the source data behind the features (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-09-24T14:05:00Z). kind label level low_per_100k May be omitted for an open-ended range. min_distinct_dates min_span_days Records must stretch across at least this many days, first to last. module mondo_id name Human-readable disease name, for reviewers. Not queried. none_of notes of operator numeric only points May be negative. provenance require_gene_text_match Default true when codes are generic LOINC panels. result Required for diagnostic_test features and for LOINC-coded phenotype features. review Clinical sign-off. Recorded only; not enforced. reviewer rules Level 2a only. CP fires if ANY rule fires. schema_version Version of THIS schema the file conforms to, e.g. 0.2.0 score Level 2b only. search_mode slug Short lowercase hyphenated disease name used in file names, e.g. xlh, fabry. source Which pipeline run or reference produced the range. specificity_grade How specific the feature is to the target disease, from S1 (confirmatory) to S5 (incidental). L1 disjuncts may only use S1 features. supersedes Previous cp_name, if any. text_terms Names and synonyms for what the feature describes (a disease, a finding, a test or a drug), for a future text-search (NLP) step. threshold title umbrella_codes units UCUM units the threshold applies to. Strongly recommended for numeric. value value_concepts qualitative only: accepted answers (e.g. LOINC LA6576-8 Positive). value_high between only vocabulary within

docs.title: Enumerations
docs.text: Enumeration Description CodeSystem CP-side vocabulary names. CPLevel How a CP's features combine into a flag. The level decides which logic block the CP carries: disjuncts (L1), rules (L2A) or score (L2B); L3 has none yet. FlagRateBasis Where the numbers in an expected flag rate come from. Module The evidence domain a feature belongs to. Drives which OMOP tables are searched and which vocabularies are allowed. ResultKind Whether a result is compared with a threshold or matched against a set of accepted answers. ResultOperator How a numeric result is compared: with a fixed threshold, a fixed range, or the normal range recorded with the result. ReviewDecision The outcome of a clinical review of a CP. SearchMode Which patients a CP searches: the whole dataset, or only those with an umbrella code. SpecificityGrade How specific a feature is to the target disease. The grade decides what counts as safe alone in L1.

docs.text: Name of the CP version, built from the disease entity, level and version. Format: <disease_entity_id>-<slug>_<level>_v<major>.<minor>, where <disease_entity_id> is disease.disease_entity_id and <slug> is disease.slug, e.g. RAPID000123-xlh_L1_v1.0.

docs.title: Slot: curation_record_version
docs.text: Version of the curation record (keyed by mondo_id) this CP was built from. Recorded, not queried.

docs.title: Slot: disease_entity_id
docs.text: Opaque id of the disease entity, RAPID + exactly six digits, e.g. RAPID000123. Minted by Mendelian. Every CP for the entity carries the same id, across levels and versions. It does not depend on Mondo, so it stays the same when the anchor Mondo id is obsoleted or merged.

docs.title: Slot: disjuncts
docs.text: Level 1 only.

docs.title: Slot: features
docs.text: Atomic evidence items. Logic blocks reference them by id.

docs.title: Slot: genetic
docs.text: Required for genetic_finding features.

docs.title: Slot: high_per_100k
docs.text: Required unless basis is none.

docs.title: Slot: hpo_id
docs.text: Phenotype features: the HPO term this realises (annotation only, not queried).

docs.title: Slot: include_descendants
docs.text: Default true for a feature's main codes, false for result value and unit codes. SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm expand via CONCEPT_ANCESTOR; ICD10CM expands by code prefix.

docs.title: Slot: include_personal_history
docs.text: diagnostic_code and coded phenotype features only. Default true: also count observation rows recording the patient's own history of the condition. Set false to count only direct records.

docs.title: Slot: included_mondo_ids
docs.text: Every Mondo id that constitutes this disease entity, mondo_id included. Defaults to [mondo_id]. Recorded, not queried.

docs.title: Slot: kg_extracted_at
docs.text: When Mendelian extracted the source data behind the features (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-09-24T14:05:00Z).

docs.title: Slot: low_per_100k
docs.text: May be omitted for an open-ended range.

docs.title: Slot: operator
docs.text: numeric only

docs.title: Slot: points
docs.text: May be negative.

docs.title: rapid_cp_schema
docs.text:
Schema for RAPID computable phenotype (CP) logic files, named <cp_name>.yaml, e.g. RAPID000123-xlh_L1_v1.0.yaml. Data-model-independent. Says WHAT counts as evidence (features, coded in source vocabularies: ICD10CM, SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, ...) and HOW the evidence combines (Level 1 disjuncts, Level 2a rules, Level 2b score). Every disjunct / rule / score item carries a stable id (d1, r2, s3) that is reported back as the flag reason.

URI: https://mendelian.co/schemas/rapid-cp-logic

docs.title: Slot: require_gene_text_match
docs.text: Default true when codes are generic LOINC panels.

docs.title: Slot: result
docs.text: Required for diagnostic_test features and for LOINC-coded phenotype features.

docs.title: Slot: review
docs.text: Clinical sign-off. Recorded only; not enforced.

docs.title: Slot: rules
docs.text: Level 2a only. CP fires if ANY rule fires.

docs.title: Slot: schema_version
docs.text: Version of THIS schema the file conforms to, e.g. 0.2.0

docs.title: Slot: score
docs.text: Level 2b only.

docs.title: Slot: slug
docs.text: Short lowercase hyphenated disease name used in file names, e.g. xlh, fabry.

docs.title: Slot: source
docs.text: Which pipeline run or reference produced the range.

docs.title: Slot: specificity_grade
docs.text: How specific the feature is to the target disease, from S1 (confirmatory) to S5 (incidental). L1 disjuncts may only use S1 features.

docs.title: Slot: supersedes
docs.text: Previous cp_name, if any.

docs.title: Slot: text_terms
docs.text: Names and synonyms for what the feature describes (a disease, a finding, a test or a drug), for a future text-search (NLP) step.

docs.title: Slot: units
docs.text: UCUM units the threshold applies to. Strongly recommended for numeric.

docs.title: Slot: value_concepts
docs.text: qualitative only: accepted answers (e.g. LOINC LA6576-8 Positive).

docs.title: Slot: value_high
docs.text: between only
